issues.issue: Which legal test applies to the equivalency of a foreign offence under IRPA s. 36(1)(c) (Garcia versus the essential-elements approach)?
issues.applicant_position: Equivalency is not dispositive, but the officer must consider the essential elements of the Canadian offence.
issues.respondent_position: Garcia is not dispositive; s. 36(1)(c) requires analysing whether the foreign facts meet the Canadian offence's essential elements.
issues.result_text: Court need not decide the Garcia divergence; officer's analysis was flawed under either approach.

issues.issue: Did the officer reasonably find that the applicant's US perjury conduct would be Canadian perjury under Criminal Code s. 131?
issues.applicant_position: Canadian perjury is narrower, covering only statements in court or before authorities, so ss. 139-140 do not apply; officer only compared titles.
issues.respondent_position: Canadian perjury is not limited to court declarations, so the essential elements match; Sosa supports equivalency.
issues.result_text: Officer did not engage with essential elements; applicant was not shown to commit Canadian perjury, so the decision is unreasonable.
